findings.claim: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the requireNonNull call with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and gets encoded as '<prefix>:null', or causes a later NPE.

verifier.reason: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:72-73, the constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and concatenated as "<prefix>:null" in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117 (or left null for downstream callers).

findings.claim: The isAccessTokenId matcher throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for prefixes shorter than 5 characters instead of returning false.

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-485, isAccessTokenId splits item on ':' and calls items[0].substring(3, 5) at line 483 without checking items[0].length(). Any two-part string whose prefix before ':' has fewer than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

findings.claim: The isAccessTokenId matcher extracts the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5). The grant shortcut sits at positions 4-5 of the 2+2+2 prefix, so the correct call is substring(4, 6).

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483, isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut using items[0].substring(3, 5), whereas DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:78-81 encodes and decodes the 6-character prefix as sessionType (0, 2), tokenType (2, 4), and grantType at substring(4, 6).

findings.claim: The isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic: it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected grant shortcut, so it rejects correct tokens and accepts wrong grant shortcuts.

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483, isAccessTokenId checks `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` without negation, so it returns false when the extracted substring matches expectedGrantShortcut and falls through to accept non-matching values when the UUID part matches.

findings.claim: The Dependabot label 'area/dependencies' does not exist.

verifier.reason: Although .github/dependabot.yml:12 and .github/dependabot.yml:23 configure 'area/dependencies' and it is also listed in .github/teams.yml:55 (and as 'dependencies' in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml:43), GitHub repository labels are managed in GitHub's external service rather than defined in the repository, so the source here cannot settle whether the label actually exists. Moreover, the patch only modifies OIDC Java/test files and does not touch .github/dependabot.yml.

findings.claim: The lazy/hot-deploy refresh paths in getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 106-137) add entries without the duplicate-shortcut check that postInit performs, so a custom grant can overwrite an existing shortcut mapping.

verifier.reason: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:106-137, neither lazy refresh path (getShortcutByGrantType at lines 106-119 nor getGrantTypeByShortcut at lines 121-137) performs the duplicate-shortcut validation done in postInit (lines 82-85). Specifically, getShortcutByGrantType unconditionally calls grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) at line 113, allowing a dynamically deployed custom grant with a colliding shortcut to silently overwrite an existing shortcut mapping.

findings.claim: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, and the patch uses both inconsistently: OAuth2GrantType.Context reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, while grants and TokenManager write Constants.GRANT_TYPE.

verifier.reason: While Constants.GRANT_TYPE aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE (Constants.java:206-207), the usage is consistent rather than inconsistent: OAuth2GrantType.Context reads the OAuth2 HTTP form parameter via formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) (OAuth2GrantType.java:102), whereas every ClientSessionContext write (e.g., TokenManager.java:248, OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109) and its reader (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57) consistently use Constants.GRANT_TYPE per its documented role as a ClientSessionContext note key.
